{{Short description|Classification method for personality psychology assessment data sources}}
'''LOTS''' is an acronym, suggested by [[Raymond Cattell|Cattell]] in 1957 and later elaborated by Block, to provide a broad classification of data source for [[personality psychology]] assessment.<ref name="ozer" />{{Rp|673}} Each data source has its advantage and disadvantage. Research on personality commonly employ different data source so as to represent better the pattern of one's distinctive features.<ref name="cattell1973" /><ref name="cattell1977" />
* L-data, refer to the life-outcome data, such as age, education, income,<ref name="handbook" />{{Rp|481}} student grades at school, criminal and conviction record<ref name="cervone" />{{Rp|13}}
* O-data, refer to observational data, such as observer rating from friends and family
* T-data, refer to standardised and objective [[Experiment|test]] measurement, such as scored test, physiological response, [[reaction time]]s (RT), [[Implicit-association test|implicit association test]] (IAT)
* S-data, refer to [[Self-report study|self-reports]], such as [[questionnaire]]s, [[personality test]], [[structured interview]]<ref name="handbook" />{{Rp|481}}
